From 7ec03e60ef81c19b5d3a46dd070ee966774b860f Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Nicolas Iooss <nicolas.iooss_linux@m4x.org>
Date: Sat, 10 Sep 2016 13:59:49 -0300
Subject: [PATCH] [media] ite-cir: initialize use_demodulator before using it

Function ite_set_carrier_params() uses variable use_demodulator after
having initialized it to false in some if branches, but this variable is
never set to true otherwise.

This bug has been found using clang -Wsometimes-uninitialized warning
flag.

Fixes: 620a32bba4a2 ("[media] rc: New rc-based ite-cir driver for
several ITE CIRs")

Signed-off-by: Nicolas Iooss <nicolas.iooss_linux@m4x.org>
Signed-off-by: Mauro Carvalho Chehab <mchehab@s-opensource.com>

diff --git a/drivers/media/rc/ite-cir.c b/drivers/media/rc/ite-cir.c
index c5e8e3885766..367b28bed627 100644
--- a/drivers/media/rc/ite-cir.c
+++ b/drivers/media/rc/ite-cir.c
@@ -261,6 +261,8 @@ static void ite_set_carrier_params(struct ite_dev *dev)
 
 			if (allowance > ITE_RXDCR_MAX)
 				allowance = ITE_RXDCR_MAX;
+
+			use_demodulator = true;
 		}
 	}
 
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

**File: `drivers/media/rc/ite-cir.c`**
- The variable `use_demodulator` is now explicitly set to `true` within the `ite_set_carrier_params()` function. This change occurs after a conditional check involving the `allowance` variable, ensuring that `use_demodulator` is initialized properly before it is used later in the function.

### Relationships
- The modification addresses a bug where the `use_demodulator` variable could potentially be used uninitialized, leading to undefined behavior. The patch ensures that `use_demodulator` is set to `true` in appropriate conditions, thus resolving the warning generated by the clang compiler regarding uninitialized variables. This change is a direct fix for the issue identified in the previous commit referenced in the patch.
